newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends on firm footing, tight grip holds.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends on firm footing, tight grip holds.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended firm on Tuesday as the tight grip on the prompt physical market continued to support cargoes.
"It's a tight market that the traders are steering," one source said. He said a flurry of deals by end-users at the higher levels meant that these strong prices "can't be dismissed anymore."
Feb swaps tacked on $6 to $225/$227 a tonne and March gained the same amount to $215/$216.
Three traders were still believed to be short material for this month to one end-user.
But rumours surfaced that the end-user may have sold a cargo to one trader in order for that trader to be "circled out" of the commitment. This could not be confirmed.
One trader thought to be short the paper market was a buyer in February paper at $231, sources said.
An end-user sold a Skikda cargo to a trader at $232 cif and another sold to an end-user an open spec cargo at $226 cif for delivery by the end of the month, sources said.
Separately, Euroilstock said on Tuesday that naphtha inventories in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose 440,000 barrels from December to 27.72 million barrels in January.
That is roughly unchanged from the year-ago level of 27.65 million.
